finding.claim: dropTable ignores the error returned by Authorize(u, "dba"), so any authenticated user, regardless of role, can execute DROP TABLE via /admin/drop.
finding.source: Authenticated request to /admin/drop whose context carries a *User without the dba role (precondition; the middleware that sets the user is not in this directory).
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + t) at api.go:27, a destructive DDL operation.

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered directly to dropTable with no authorization wrapper in this file.
u := userFrom(r) loads the caller from the request context.
Authorize(u, "dba") is called but its error return is discarded.
runSQL executes regardless of whether the role check passed.
Handler returns 204 No Content, so a denied caller sees success.

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is correct in isolation but its result is ignored at the call site. vacuum (api.go:33-36) checks the error and returns 403, showing the correct pattern. userFrom (api.go:22) is an unchecked type assertion that panics on missing user; this is a crash, not a bypass. No other gate exists in this file.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is the only role check and it is never tested at the call site: api.go:26 is a bare statement whose error is discarded. vacuum (api.go:33-35) shows the correct check-and-return pattern, but dropTable does not use it. No authorization wrapper is applied at registration (api.go:44). userFrom (api.go:22) only panics on a missing user, which is a crash, not a gate. Input validation for r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 is absent, so the sink is also unparameterized, though that is not the claimed issue.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: userFrom at api.go:25, the discarded Authorize result at api.go:26, runSQL at api.go:27 running unconditionally, and the 204 response at api.go:28 are all as described, and /admin/drop is registered without a wrapper at api.go:44, so any authenticated low-privilege user reaches the DROP TABLE effect at api.go:27.

finding.claim: SQL injection in dropTable: the table name from the request is concatenated unvalidated into a DROP TABLE statement.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27, which reads both URL query string and POST form body.
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + ...) at api.go:27; runSQL is defined at api.go:41 as an empty stub, so runtime behavior is assumed to execute the string as SQL.

trace.note: Value is concatenated directly into the DROP TABLE string.
runSQL(string) is the sink; body is a stub so execution path is unverified.

finding.guards_checked: No table-name allowlist, no identifier quoting or escaping, no format or length validation. Parameter binding does not apply because identifiers cannot be bound as parameters. Reachability depends on passing the authorization check in F1, which is not enforced, so the injection is reachable by any caller who reaches the route.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize at api.go:26 is called as a bare statement, so its error return is discarded and it blocks nothing; no table-name allowlist, identifier quoting, or validation exists between r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 and runSQL at api.go:41. The only effective check is in vacuum (api.go:33-36), which is not on this path.
verdict.reason: The request value is concatenated unvalidated into "DROP TABLE " at api.go:27 and passed to runSQL (api.go:41), and the role check at api.go:26 discards its error, so any caller who reaches /admin/drop with a user in context can inject. The runSQL body is an empty stub, so actual execution is not visible here, and that caveat is the only thing keeping this from a stronger verdict.
